findings.issue: The reduction to three unknowns appeals to 'symmetry' without justification. It is valid because the six-state generator is irreducible and is invariant under simultaneously swapping link labels and channel states. Its unique stationary law is therefore swap-invariant. Re-deriving the balance equations from the stated rates confirms the result. The out-rates are 12/5, 11/10 and 3/2 from the empty, good-active and bad-active states. A channel flip maps good-active to bad-active in the other state. This reproduces all four displayed equations, the unique solution (13,37,29)/158, useful service 2·37/158 = 37/79, and the frozen-Gibbs value 9/(1+9+1) = 9/11. The stated scope, falsifying a stationary-law shortcut only, is accurate.
findings.required_fix: Add one sentence: irreducibility implies a unique stationary law, hence swap invariance, hence the symmetric ansatz is exact.

findings.issue: Re-derived and correct. The queue is 0 at each cycle start. Pre-slot backlogs sum to (k(k+1)/2 − 1) + (k+1)(k+2)/2 = k²+2k. Elapsed time is 2K(K+1). The average is K(K+1)(2K+7)/6 divided by 2K(K+1), which equals (2K+7)/12 → ∞. The peak is k+1 = O(√t), so Q(t)/t → 0. The arrival-mean limit exists along all t, not only at cycle ends. A work-conserving single server minimizes the queue pathwise, so no policy whatsoever satisfies (B2) on this input. That states the assumption gap more cleanly than 'even the work-conserving central scheduler'.
findings.required_fix: None required. Optionally, state the pathwise-optimality strengthening.

findings.issue: The gap is attributed partly to 'memoryless'. Statewise the policy is memoryless: each slot uses only the current Q_i(t), C_i(t) and fresh randomness. It is time-inhomogeneous only through the global counter. The decisive failure is 'simple': expected per-slot work is n·e^{(t+1)^2}/(t+2), and this is intrinsic to the per-slot design (see F5). 'Distributed' holds only given a common epoch, global slot synchronization, and a synchronized freeze at a resolution much finer than 1/R_t.
findings.required_fix: List the three printed requirements separately. Simple: fails, intrinsically for this design. Distributed: holds only given global synchronization and a common epoch. Memoryless: holds statewise but fails time-homogeneity.

review.scope_assessment: This is a valid but deliberately impractical scoped theorem, not a book solution. PARTIAL is the correct book-level label. Additions beyond the supplied printed text: (1) iid arrival vectors with a finite bound a_*. The book gives only long-run means; §5.3 correctly shows some temporal regularity is necessary, but iid-bounded is much stronger than necessary and excludes, for example, Poisson arrivals. (2) Finite-state irreducible Markov block fading, constant within each slot, with exact instantaneous local CSI. (3) Perfect, instantaneous, edge-exact sensing of reservation bits. (4) A common epoch, global slot synchronization, and a synchronized freeze at a resolution far below 1/R_t. (5) Real-valued access probabilities as small as 1/(1+e^{Q_iC_i}). (6) Divisible work and deterministic Q(0). (7) A time-inhomogeneous clock with n·e^{(t+1)^2}/(t+2) expected rings per slot. Time-varying rates are handled only across slots. The per-slot reset and an overwhelming clock make each slot's schedule an essentially exact Gibbs sample for the current (Q,C). The access dynamics therefore never interact with channel variation, and the problem collapses to MaxWeight with additive error under Markov modulation (Lemma 4), which is classical. The printed difficulty is the feedback among adaptive access probabilities, queues and time-varying rates without time-scale separation. That difficulty is bypassed by the architecture, not reduced. Requirement by requirement: distributed only with global synchronization and the common counter; memoryless statewise but time-inhomogeneous; simple fails, intrinsically for any per-slot near-MaxWeight design (F5). Oracle audit: there is no hidden runtime oracle or global queue maximum, but the counter acts as the surrogate for global max-weight information. Quantitatively, the backlog constant is polynomial, up to logarithmic factors, in (n, a_*, c_*, 1/ε, H, ‖Q(0)‖), so all the impracticality lives in the clock. The document's caveats are adequate in substance: PARTIAL, the cost (3), fine timing, 'simple local update is not simple low-cost scheduler', no novelty claim, and no coverage of intra-slot fading or non-iid arrivals. They become fully adequate once four overstatements are corrected (F4–F6, F10): 'implementable local rates', 'explicit constant K', the unqualified 'does not hide a maximum independent-set oracle', and 'the precise … blocker'.
review.novelty_assessment: No novelty is claimed and none was found. Every ingredient is standard: (1) heat-bath (Glauber) dynamics for the weighted hard-core model with a product-form Gibbs stationary law, i.e. the CSMA product form; (2) a Doeblin-type all-zero coalescence bound; (3) the Gibbs variational inequality, giving an additive MaxWeight loss of at most log|I(G)|; (4) a T-slot quadratic drift with a Poisson-equation correction for Markov-modulated service; and (5) a Hajek-type passage from bounded-increment negative drift to a uniform exponential moment. The one design-specific device indexes a superexponential clock to the global slot counter so that it dominates the worst-case pathwise mixing scale e^{O(t)}. This is time-scale separation by fiat: it trades global time for global queue information. It contributes no technique that transfers to the bounded-rate, time-homogeneous, intra-slot-varying setting the book is about. Positioning against Yun–Shin–Yi (cited in the document) and other CSMA, time-varying-channel or scheduling-hardness work is unverified, because no such source is supplied. Names recalled from background only, for example Jiang–Walrand, Ni–Tan–Srikant Q-CSMA, Rajagopalan–Shah–Shin and Shah–Tse–Tsitsiklis, are likewise unverified.
review.first_independent_check: An independent checker who does not reuse work/check.py should first verify the load-bearing Lemma 2→3 bridge exactly on small instances. Use the 3-vertex path, the triangle and the 4-cycle, with several weight vectors including one weight ≥ 10. Build the frozen heat-bath generator and compute the law of σ(u) from the all-zero state by exact or interval-arithmetic matrix exponential, for several (R,u). Confirm three things: (i) detailed balance and stationarity of (5); (ii) TV ≤ (1−p(w))^{⌊Ru⌋} with p(w) = e^{−n}∏_i(1+e^{w_i})^{−1}; (iii) E_{σ(u)}W ≥ W_max − log|I(G)| − W_max·TV. In the same pass, solve the full 6×6 generator of §5.1 in exact rational arithmetic without imposing the symmetry ansatz; analytically one expects (13,37,29)/158 per channel state and service 37/79. Also recompute the §5.3 cycle sums by direct recursion; one expects k²+2k per cycle and an average of (2K+7)/12. Finally, write F_t out explicitly as in F2 and re-check that (7) and (14) both hold under that single filtration.
